content.en: Inflation in the Indian economy is primarily driven by two mechanisms: **Demand-Pull Inflation**, which occurs when aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply, and **Cost-Push Inflation**, which arises from an increase in the cost of production inputs such as wages or raw materials. Additionally, **Structural Inflation** plays a significant role in developing economies due to supply chain inefficiencies and infrastructure gaps.
